item.title: The Database resource
item.description:
The api/v1alpha1 package declares the resource as Go values. kube reflects its CRD from them.

The types

The spec names the database, and says what deleting the Database does to it. The status names the Secret, and holds the conditions:

type DeletionPolicy string

const (
	Retain DeletionPolicy = "Retain"
	Delete DeletionPolicy = "Delete"
)

type DatabaseSpec struct {
	Name string `json:"name"`
	DeletionPolicy DeletionPolicy `json:"deletionPolicy,omitempty"`
}

type DatabaseStatus struct {
	SecretName string `json:"secretName,omitempty"`
	Conditions []metav1.Condition `json:"conditions,omitempty"`
}

The resource and its rules

item.title: Talking to PostgreSQL
item.description:
The postgres package provisions and drops a Database’s role and database, through one admin connection to the server.

The admin interface

The Reconciler and its finalizer call PostgreSQL through an interface, so their tests can fake it:

type Admin interface {
	Provision(ctx context.Context, name, password string) error
	Drop(ctx context.Context, name string) error
}

Both are safe to repeat: a reconcile that fails partway is run again.

The Server

Server implements Admin on a pool. It traces each statement, and injects faults before each operation:

item.title: Reconciling
item.description:
The controller package’s Reconciler brings a Database to its spec, whatever state it finds. A reconcile that fails is retried, with backoff, so each step is safe to repeat.

The Reconciler

It holds a clientset for the Secret, the Admin, and the server’s address, which the Secret hands on:

const fieldManager = "databases-controller"

type database = kube.Object[v1alpha1.DatabaseSpec, v1alpha1.DatabaseStatus]

type Reconciler struct {
	Kube kubernetes.Interface
	Admin postgres.Admin
	Host string
	Port int
}

var _ kube.Reconciler[v1alpha1.DatabaseSpec, v1alpha1.DatabaseStatus] = Reconciler{}

The steps

Reconcile reads the password, provisions the role and the database, applies the Secret, then sets Ready. An apply the API server refuses with a conflict means the Secret was deleted after it was read, so the password is rotated there and then:

item.title: Cleaning up
item.description:
The database and the role are outside the cluster, so no owner reference can garbage collect them. A finalizer keeps a deleted Database until the controller has cleaned up after it.

The finalizer

Init registers the Reconciler’s Finalize under the finalizer’s name:

const (
	serviceAccount = "/var/run/secrets/kubernetes.io/serviceaccount/"
	finalizer = "postgres.example.com/finalizer"
	scenarioAnnotation = "postgres.example.com/failure-scenario"
)

kube.Finalize(finalizer, rec.Finalize),

The controller adds the finalizer to each Database. Once one is deleted, it calls Finalize, and removes the finalizer when Finalize succeeds, which lets the API server delete the Database.

item.title: Init
item.description:
The settings

Everything Init reads, in one struct:

type settings struct {
	Connection kube.Connection
	Controller kube.Settings
	Admin *pgxpool.Config
	Host string
	Port int
	Probes httphealth.Settings
	TrustedPrefix string
}

config.Struct sources and checks each one. A bad one makes Init fail, and the controller exits 78, naming its variable:

func readSettings(ctx context.Context, s *humus.Setup) (settings, error) {
	env := func(name string) config.Value[string] { return config.Env(s.Process.Environment, name) }
	read := readFile(s.Host.FS)

	return config.Struct(func(r *config.Resolver) settings {
		tokenFile := r.Get(env("KUBERNETES_TOKEN_FILE").Default(serviceAccount + "token").Validate(func(name string) error {
			_, err := readToken(s.Host.FS, name)
			return err
		}))

		k := kube.DefaultSettings()
		k.Name = r.Get(env("CONTROLLER_NAME").Default("databases-controller").Validate(kube.CheckName))
		k.Namespace = r.Get(env("CONTROLLER_NAMESPACE").Default(k.Namespace).Validate(kube.CheckWatchNamespace))
		k.Workers = r.Get(env("CONTROLLER_WORKERS").Parse(strconv.Atoi).Default(k.Workers).Validate(kube.CheckWorkers))
		k.Resync = r.Get(env("CONTROLLER_RESYNC").Parse(time.ParseDuration).Default(k.Resync).Validate(kube.CheckResync))
		k.LeaderElection.Namespace = r.Get(env("POD_NAMESPACE").Validate(kube.CheckNamespace))
		k.LeaderElection.Identity = r.Get(env("POD_NAME").Validate(kube.CheckIdentity))

		return settings{
			Connection: kube.Connection{
				Server: net.JoinHostPort(
					r.Get(env("KUBERNETES_SERVICE_HOST").Validate(checkAPIServerHost)),
					r.Get(env("KUBERNETES_SERVICE_PORT").Validate(checkAPIServerPort)),
				),
				TLS: r.Get(env("KUBERNETES_CA_FILE").Default(serviceAccount + "ca.crt").Parse(read).Parse(certPool).Map(trusting).Validate(kube.CheckTLS)),
				Token: func(context.Context) (string, error) {
					return readToken(s.Host.FS, tokenFile)
				},
			},
			Controller: k,
			Admin: r.Get(env("POSTGRES_ADMIN_DSN_FILE").Parse(read).Parse(adminDSN)),
			Host: r.Get(env("POSTGRES_HOST").Validate(notEmpty)),
			Port: r.Get(env("POSTGRES_PORT").Parse(strconv.Atoi).Default(5432).Validate(checkPostgresPort)),
			Probes: httphealth.Settings{
				Addr: r.Get(env("PROBES_ADDR").Validate(httphealth.CheckAddr)),
				TLS: r.Get(env("PROBES_TLS_PEM_FILE").Parse(pemTLS(s.Host.FS)).Validate(httphealth.CheckTLS)),
			},
			TrustedPrefix: r.Get(env("FAULT_TRUSTED_NAMESPACE_PREFIX").Default("")),
		}
	}).Read(ctx)
}
Variable What it is Default
KUBERNETES_SERVICE_HOST, KUBERNETES_SERVICE_PORT the API server, which the kubelet sets in every container required
KUBERNETES_CA_FILE, KUBERNETES_TOKEN_FILE the API server’s CA, and the service account’s token the service account’s, mounted in the pod
CONTROLLER_NAME the controller’s name, its Lease’s, and its field manager databases-controller
CONTROLLER_NAMESPACE the one namespace it watches every namespace
CONTROLLER_WORKERS, CONTROLLER_RESYNC how many Databases are reconciled at once, and how often every one is reconciled again kube.DefaultSettings()'
POD_NAMESPACE, POD_NAME the Lease’s namespace, and this replica’s identity in it required
POSTGRES_ADMIN_DSN_FILE a file holding the admin connection’s DSN, its password included required
POSTGRES_HOST, POSTGRES_PORT the server’s address, as a client reaches it, which each Secret holds required, and 5432
PROBES_ADDR, PROBES_TLS_PEM_FILE the probes’ address, and a file holding their certificate and key, PEM required
FAULT_TRUSTED_NAMESPACE_PREFIX the namespace prefix whose Databases’ scenarios are trusted none
FAULT_MAX_DELAY the longest delay a scenario injects 10s

item.title: Testing
item.description:
A unit test of the Reconciler

The Reconciler takes a clientset and the Admin interface, so its unit tests give it client-go’s fake clientset and a fake Admin, which records what it was given:

type fakeAdmin struct {
	provisions []provision
	provisionErr error
	databases map[string]bool
	drops []string
	dropErr error
}

func (a *fakeAdmin) Provision(_ context.Context, name, password string) error {
	a.provisions = append(a.provisions, provision{name: name, password: password})
	return a.provisionErr
}

func (a *fakeAdmin) Drop(_ context.Context, name string) error {
	a.drops = append(a.drops, name)
	if a.dropErr != nil {
		return a.dropErr
	}
	delete(a.databases, name)
	return nil
}

func newReconciler(kc *kubefake.Clientset, admin *fakeAdmin) controller.Reconciler {
	return controller.Reconciler{Kube: kc, Admin: admin, Host: "postgres.databases.svc", Port: 5432}
}

Each test reconciles a Database, and checks what the Admin was given, the Secret, and the status:

item.title: Deploying
item.description:
The image

The controller is built static onto a distroless, non-root base:

FROM docker.io/library/golang:1.27.3-trixie@sha256:fbb7ae40b62ff8afe31662df570d39b4f5052ac32b90dae8e60d7657a20a74f4 AS build
WORKDIR /src
COPY go.mod go.sum ./
COPY kube/go.mod kube/go.sum kube/
COPY example/kube/databases/go.mod example/kube/databases/go.sum example/kube/databases/
RUN go -C example/kube/databases mod download
COPY . .
RUN CGO_ENABLED=0 go -C example/kube/databases build -trimpath -ldflags=-s -o /out/databases .

FROM gcr.io/distroless/static-debian13:nonroot@sha256:d62067879de890a1def9da0e7766b7d20810a5e5555cef8506b752437d7a3e88
COPY --from=build /out/databases /databases
USER 65532:65532
ENTRYPOINT ["/databases"]

Build it from the repository’s root, since the module replaces humus and kube with their directories:

item.title: Observing
item.description:
Opening Grafana

up.sh generates Grafana’s admin password into the grafana-admin Secret. Read it, then forward Grafana’s port:

kubectl --context kind-kind --namespace databases get secret grafana-admin \
 --output jsonpath='{.data.password}' | base64 --decode
kubectl --context kind-kind --namespace databases port-forward service/grafana 3000:3000

Sign in at http://localhost:3000 as admin.

A reconcile’s trace

Apply the Database in deploy/kind/database.yaml, as Deploying shows. In Explore, choose Tempo and find its reconciles by its namespace and name:

{resource.service.name="databases" && span.k8s.namespace.name="default" && span.humus.kube.object.name="orders"}
Span What it is
reconcile Database the reconcile, a root span, with k8s.namespace.name and humus.kube.object.name
SELECT pg_roles, CREATE ROLE, ALTER ROLE, SELECT pg_database, CREATE DATABASE, ALTER DATABASE the Server’s statements as it provisions, with db.query.summary and no SQL text
DROP DATABASE, DROP ROLE the statements of a Finalize whose policy is Delete
GET, PATCH each request to the API server, from otelhttp, such as reading the Secret and applying it

So a reconcile’s trace holds everything it did. A test of the App checks it:

item.title: Production-ready
item.description:
The controller meets each item. Check your own controller against them:

Item How Where
Every setting sourced and checked; a bad one exits 78, naming its variable config.Struct, kube’s checks and the controller’s own The settings
No secret in the environment, the logs or the spans the admin DSN, the service account’s token and CA, and the probes’ key are files read through s.Host.FS. A role’s password reaches PostgreSQL as a SCRAM verifier, and a statement’s span carries its summary, never its SQL. A test of the App checks that no password, DSN or token is in a span, a record or a metric The secrets, as files, Keeping the password out of the SQL, Keeping credentials out of the spans
Certificates renewed without a restart the probes’ certificate is served through GetCertificate, by a small helper of the walkthrough’s own that reads its file again when it changes. The token’s file is read each time the Client asks, so a rotated one is picked up The probes, The Connection
Available through a lost replica two replicas share the Lease, and the standby takes over when the leader stops. A rollout starts a new replica before it stops an old one, and a PodDisruptionBudget of minAvailable: 1 The Settings and the Lease, The Deployment, The disruption budget
Ready only once its caches have synced Synced as readiness, on an HTTPS probes port The probes
A rollout loses nothing SIGTERM finishes the reconciles in flight and releases the Lease, in a grace period of 20s, and terminationGracePeriodSeconds is 30. The next leader lists every Database again The grace period, main
Reconciling again is harmless the Secret is the password’s source of truth, so every reconcile sets the same one. The role and the database are ensured, and the drops are IF EXISTS The password, Provisioning, Dropping
Deleting cleans up, as the Database says the finalizer holds a deleted Database until Finalize has dropped what its deletionPolicy says to. The Secret is deleted with it, as the Database controls it The finalizer, The Secret
Least privilege a ClusterRole that watches and patches Databases and applies Secrets, and a Role for its own Lease and no other. A non-root container, on a read-only root filesystem, with every capability dropped RBAC, The Deployment
Observable traces, logs and metrics over OTLP, and rules for failing, panicking and stuck reconciles, a backlog and restarts, on humus’s own instruments, and a dashboard Observing
Failures say why a failed step sets Ready to False, with a reason naming the step, PostgresUnavailable or SecretApplyFailed The conditions
Failures are rehearsed the failure injection cases The failure injection cases
Safe by default deletionPolicy defaults to Retain, and name is immutable. No namespace’s scenarios are trusted The resource and its rules, Trusting a namespace’s scenarios
